limitations: Native Linux and Windows test execution is unavailable; cross compilation is not execution.
One requested 30-second sample per workload/stage; no statistical performance trend is claimed. Go may reach its iteration ceiling sooner for extremely small operations.
Raw source snapshots, cached corpora, profiles and matching binaries are local and ignored. Reports retain hashes and command lineage.
Numeric oversize benchmark MB/s describes supplied input extent; the width rejection intentionally does not scan that input and MB/s is not processing throughput.
Tests and subtests are Go event counts, not independent regression counts.

The initial campaign labels are diagnostic runs before the after benchmarks; final-campaign labels are the final fuzz phase after the retained benchmarks. The intermediate after benchmarks preceded the profile-informed short-URL bound optimization and remain in the attempt history.
The projection fuzzer compares separate Core public doors with a shared structural scanner; explicit boundary tables supply the independent limit expectations.
